# Kunjar Bhaduri

> Full text of the home page, except the track-record figures. Those stay on https://kunjarbhaduri.com/ and are not copied here. No street address.


## https://kunjarbhaduri.com/

CTO, CIO and Chief AI Officer.

Kunjar Bhaduri.

Technology turnarounds for financial services and PE-backed companies.

Interim, fractional or permanent. Dallas, Texas.

I'm a CTO who works with private equity sponsors and leadership teams in financial services and other regulated businesses. I'm open to permanent, interim and fractional CTO, CIO and Chief AI Officer roles, and to technology operating partner and board work. Recruiters and sponsors can contact me through LinkedIn.

I'm usually brought in when technology has started to limit the business: a failing program, a client ready to leave, a platform nobody fully understands, or a cyber incident. My first job is to find out what is actually broken and who owns each decision, then set priorities the business can execute.

The track-record section names Broadridge, Wipro Opus and Cognizant. The figures in that section are on the page and are not repeated in this file.

AI is now part of the same operating work. My work on Autonomy Ladder focuses on reference implementations of controls for AI agents in regulated businesses: what the system may do, how that limit is tested, and what happens when a control fails.

Bhaduri Advisory. Strategy, operations and technology for founders.

I have run P&Ls and technology teams in financial services for most of my career. I am now independent, and through Bhaduri Advisory I put that experience to work for founders in Dallas-Fort Worth, as a fractional or interim operator alongside the founder.

What I can do for a founder: company strategy and go-to-market (work out who the customer is, how to reach them, and which partners or alliances can help; support in investor meetings); running the business day to day (what to source and how to buy it, supplier terms, budgets, pricing and weekly priorities); hiring and keeping good people (which leaders and roles are needed next, help hiring them, and the management habits that keep them); technology, product and AI (review the architecture and AI-written code before growth makes problems costly, and get data and models ready for real customers).

A good fit is a founder working on a real customer problem who wants an experienced operator involved. I am most useful when the problem touches technology, operations and commercial decisions at once.

Software companies building fast with AI: teams shipping quickly with AI need an experienced look at the architecture, security and delivery before customers or investors look closely. I review the architecture and the AI-written code, and help the team fix what growth would otherwise make costly.

Companies training AI and analytics models: I help teams check their data, test and monitor their models, and get from a promising model to a first customer pilot.

Founders who need a business operator: strategy, partnerships and alliances, hiring, budgets and supplier choices, as a fractional or interim operator alongside the founder.

How we could work together: start with a focused review or a defined project; it can grow into an ongoing or interim role. Focused review: two weeks, fixed fee, one defined question (go-to-market, product architecture, hiring and supplier priorities), ends with a written recommendation and next steps. Fractional retainer: a few hours a week, billed monthly, ongoing strategy, operating or technology leadership, with decisions and ownership agreed up front. Project or interim: scoped to an outcome, such as a go-to-market plan, key hires, a supplier strategy, or a product ready to launch.

On terms: Open to equity for the right founder and business. Cash-plus-equity, project fees and monthly retainers also work. Scope, time and terms are agreed per company before starting, and priced once the work is defined.

I'm based in Dallas. Most of my career has been in financial services: wealth management, capital markets, securities services, cards, lending and mortgage.

Sectors: wealth management, capital markets, securities services, cards, lending, mortgage.

## https://kunjarbhaduri.com/work-with-me/

Work with me. Five ways to bring Kunjar Bhaduri in, from a fixed-fee technology review of a portfolio company to a seat on your leadership team. All of them start with a 15-minute call: https://calendly.com/kunjarbhaduri/intro

1. Private equity sponsors: Tech Health snapshot for portfolio companies. A fixed-scope review of how healthy a company's technology is, written for the sponsor and the CEO. Built for companies that run on software but do not sell it. For operating partners, deal teams and portfolio CEOs, before close, after close or before an exit. You get a read-only review of the main systems, cloud accounts, user access, backups and recovery, key vendors and contracts, and any code the company owns (nothing is changed in the company's environment); short interviews with the CEO, CFO, whoever runs IT and the main outside IT provider; a Tech Health Index score from 0 to 100 built from the same areas for every company; a written readout ranking risks by effect on cash, customers and the investment plan, with an owner and a rough cost and timing to fix each; and a one-hour readout meeting. Timeline: about three weeks from read-only access to the readout. After the snapshot: portfolio monitoring (a refreshed score and a review with each company's leadership every quarter) and CTO on call (a senior technology leader for vendor renewals, incidents, key hires and add-on diligence). Fees: the snapshot is a fixed fee, quoted after a 15-minute call; monitoring is billed per company per month; CTO on call is a monthly retainer.

2. Leadership teams and boards: fractional or interim CTO, CIO or Chief AI Officer. For PE-backed and financial services companies that are between technology leaders, in a turnaround, rebuilding a platform, or not yet ready for a full-time hire. Starts with a 100-day plan: in the first two weeks, follow one process the business cannot afford to lose and find its owner, the vendor that can interrupt it and when it was last restored; by day 30, an agreed cost and headcount baseline, decision rights and an incident escalation path; by day 60, one bottleneck fixed, a tested restore and a short list of remaining risks; by day 100, a funded roadmap, named owners for open decisions and a handover, including help hiring a permanent leader. Interim roles are full time for an agreed period. Fractional roles are a set number of days each week, billed monthly. Also open to permanent roles.

3. Investors, consultants and research teams: expert calls and short consulting projects, through expert networks or direct. Topics: wealth management and advisor technology; investment operations and post-trade processing; customer and investor communications in regulated industries; lending and mortgage technology; IT services and outsourcing pricing and how AI agents change services contracts; evaluating and rolling out AI coding tools; AI agent governance in banks and other regulated firms; cloud migration, cyber recovery and operational resilience; tokenization, stablecoins and settlement from the payments architecture and operations side; technology diligence and the first 100 days at a PE portfolio company. Will not discuss confidential information of any current or former employer or client, anything under a confidentiality agreement, or any company where a call would conflict with a current engagement. Calls are usually one hour. Hourly rate on request.

4. Boards, risk leaders and AI teams: AI governance advisory and advisory boards, using Autonomy Ladder (https://autonomy-ladder.io/), an open-source framework from A0 (read and recommend only) to A4 (production with monitoring and escalation). You get a map of each AI action in a workflow to a rung, control tests against the real system (expired approval, blocked write, missing audit event) checked against the system of record, a plain-language board briefing, and for advisory boards a standing seat. The ladder is a design discipline for governing agent authority; it does not establish regulatory compliance or replace model validation. A governance review covers one system or workflow and takes about two weeks. Free self-score: https://autonomy-ladder.io/assessment

5. Founders: founder advisory through Bhaduri Advisory, as described on the home page. A focused review runs two weeks for a fixed fee and can grow into a fractional retainer or a project or interim role. Open to equity for the right founder and business.

Not sure which fits: book 15 minutes, message on LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/in/kunjarbhaduri/), or use the form on the home page.
